messages:
elinor: FYI escalation from @acme — they hit repeated disconnects during streaming responses, often with a truncated JSON object in the final chunk. They say reconnecting sometimes causes duplicate partial messages and extra billing for repeated tokens. Ticket #C-2026.
kevin: can you paste the raw client logs and headers they used?
elinor: pasted below. They repro with our Python SDK async iterator. main points: long response (~800 tokens), connection drops ~at token ~612, client reconnects and yields a duplicate partial chunk followed by nothing. They supplied this snippet.
elinor: ```python
# repro (simplified)
from redwood import StreamingClient

async def run():
    cl = StreamingClient(api_key=..., streaming=True)
    async for chunk in cl.stream("gpt-open-large", prompt="<long prompt>"):
        print(chunk)

# they call run() in FastAPI background task, using uvicorn --reload
```
ajay: logs?
elinor: logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:21.123Z] CONNECT /v1/streams -> 101 Switching Protocols
[2026-03-15T12:01:22.981Z] TOKEN_REFRESH event id=xyz
[2026-03-15T12:03:45.452Z] connection closed by client: ECONNRESET
[2026-03-15T12:03:45.553Z] client reconnected, resumed seq=612
[2026-03-15T12:03:45.554Z] partial_frame: '{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...", "role":"assistant"}},'  // truncated
[2026-03-15T12:03:46.001Z] duplicate_seq detected: 612
```
kevin: couple of notes: 1) they run token refresh on a separate thread (FastAPI background task) which might be racing with the SSE reconnect logic; 2) uvicorn reload/worker model sometimes interacts poorly with asyncio EventSource/AbortController patterns.
james: @kevin can you try to reproduce locally with an auth rotation around the same time as a disconnect? If its client-side, maybe a retry race sends overlapping resume requests causing duplicate token billing.
kevin: will try. hypothesis: when the client re-establishes, it may replay the last buffered chunk and our resume logic accepts it again because seq uniqueness check is done after partial assembly. That could produce duplicated partial frames and double-charge if we re-count tokens on retried frames.
elinor: ACME reports it happened on both Python and Node, but repro easiest on their Python app. They also reported high-latency spikes just before the disconnect (300-800ms per token).
ajay: tagging eng-runtime for potential server-side edge: @kevin any chance our resume window may accept overlapping KV cache updates causing the same tokens to be emitted twice? Also check billing pipeline idempotency.
kevin: good call. i'll instrument the resume path to log resume_offset and whether tokens for that offset were already emitted. Also lean on billing team: we should ensure we dedupe billing events by (request_id, seq) when resume occurs.
support-bot: Ticket C-2026 status set to escalated -> eng-runtime. SLA window: 48h.
james: quick mitigation to propose to ACME: disable client auto-retry (set auto_reconnect=False) and add client-side dedupe on chunk.seq for now. If they can tolerate a single failed request, at least they won't see duplicates or extra billing.
elinor: they asked for a short repro script we can run in our env. kevin — can you paste the failing test once you have it?
kevin: yes. i'll post a minimal pytest that simulates token rotation during a midstream disconnect. expecting to have results by EOD.
ajay: if we confirm server accepts duplicate resume frames, plan: 1) quick server-side guard to ignore exact duplicate seq emissions for 24h; 2) longer fix: make resume handshake include resume_nonce and have server dedupe on (request_id, resume_nonce, seq).
kevin: agree. will open a follow-up PR for a hard guard and unit tests. marking this thread for postmortem if billing impact > $100 in last 7 days.
elinor: ACME also wants us to check for JSON truncation — they saw malformed final chunk that broke their JSON parser. can we ensure we never cut UTF-8 codepoints in half when sending frames?
kevin: we already try to break on unicode boundaries but will audit. might be related to partial flush when connection closes mid-emit.
james: good. please keep ticket updated. tagging @billing to review charges for C-2026.
support-bot: Billing alert: Potential duplicate charge detected for customer ACME between 2026-03-12 and 2026-03-15. Flagged for manual review.
elinor: thanks everyone — i'll message ACME with short workaround and ETA for eng triage. updating ticket.
